system_config.target_register: 합쇼체 (~습니다) in every prose sentence, as in every post on this blog

task: Rewrite inputs.content_markdown as a natural Korean technical blog post and write its Korean headline. Translate meaning, not sentence structure.
constraints: naturalness: Rebuild each paragraph in Korean word order. Split or merge sentences where Korean reads better, but keep every claim, its conditions, and the order of the argument. Never add or drop a claim.
register: Use 합쇼체 in every prose sentence, the conclusion checklist included. Questions to the reader end in ~ㄹ까요? or ~습니까?.

terminology: Render every term in inputs.terms as its term_ko, or keep the English original when keep_english is true. On the first use in the body, put the English original in parentheses: 전파 속성(propagation). Never put English glosses in the title.

avoid_translationese: Avoid patterns common in translated and AI-written Korean: heavy metaphors (봉합, 청사진, 적신호, 신호탄), cleft sentences (핵심은 ~, 관건은 ~, 중요한 것은 ~), inverted closings (~하는 이유입니다.), and English-style predicates (따라갑니다, 따라가 봅니다). Prefer verbs to chains of nouns joined by 의, and drop pronouns such as 그것 or 이것 where Korean does not need them. Do not tell the reader what to notice (~라는 점에 주목해야 합니다, 짚어 둘 만합니다, 눈여겨볼 필요가 있습니다); state the fact itself. Do not end a section with a one-sentence wrap-up that opens with 결국, 요컨대, or 다시 말해.

preserve: Keep every <!-- sec:... --> anchor, code fence, language tag, inline code span, URL, and table structure exactly as given. Inside code, translate only comments into Korean; never change code.
tables: Translate every table cell and keep cells short. Keep the 📊 at the start of table titles.
headings: Translate headings and keep their number prefix (## 1. ...).

title: Write a Korean blog headline, not a translation of inputs.title. Choose the form that fits: a symptom the reader runs into -> '…하는 이유' or '왜 …할까?'; how something works -> '…는 어떻게 동작할까' or '… 이해하기'. At most 40 characters, one promise, the words a reader would search for, no parentheses or English glosses, no colon subtitle, and no first-person framing ('도입기', '개선기').

content_markdown.description: Full Korean markdown body with every anchor preserved
